Prepare data and choose power for WGCNA

Source: R/prepare_WGCNA.R
prepare_WGCNA.Rd

Prepare input data for WGCNA (format, QC), then choose the appropriate soft thresholding power for network construction, by analysing scale free topology with different soft thresholding powers.

Usage

prepare_WGCNA(
  se_obj,
  assay,
  networkType = "signed",
  RsquaredCut = 0.8,
  MeanConnectivity = 100,
  powers = NULL,
  fontsize = 8,
  ...
)

Arguments

se_obj

A SummarizedExperiment object. Data normalised to time point 0 can be in the second assay slot, created by normalise_to_start(). Features can be pre-filtered, e.g. by residual variance calculated by decomp_variance(), to remove noisy features before running WGCNA.

assay

The assay to use in the SummarizedExperiment object: a numeric index or character name, e.g. 1 or "orig" for original data, 2 or "norm" for time 0 normalised data. (Required, no default.)

networkType

Parameter of WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold() (default is "signed")

RsquaredCut

Parameter of WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold() (default is 0.8)

MeanConnectivity

Line of mean connectivity (default is 100)

powers

Parameter of WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold() (default: NULL, auto-assigned as seq(1, 20))

fontsize

Font size for the plot (default is 8)

...

Additional parameters to be passed to WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold()

Value

A list containing results of the scale-free topology fit indices with different powers, WGCNA's powerEstimate, a custom custom_powerEstimate based on the signed scale-free topology fit, network type, and prepared input data used for reuse in run_WGCNA().

The custom estimate selects the lowest power whose signed scale-free topology fit exceeds RsquaredCut, consistent with the signed-R-squared panel in the diagnostic plot.

References

https://github.com/edo98811/WGCNA_official_documentation/

Examples

data(example_obj)

wgcna_input <- prepare_WGCNA(example_obj, assay = 2, powers = seq(1, 30),
    networkType = "signed", RsquaredCut = 0.8)
